title: Extraction of Cobalt (II) with Rhodanide Ions and Dimethylformamide
author: A.Sh. Giyasov, Rakhmatullaeva N.T., A.A. Shokhakimova, Rakhmatov U.N., Otayuziea V.U
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare acidic sample with reagents
steps.instruction: In a test tube, place the aqueous sample, adjust to a strongly acidic pH, add an excess of thiocyanate ions and dimethylformamide (DMF) to the solution.

steps.title: Extract cobalt into chloroform
steps.instruction: Add chloroform to the tube so that the aqueous‑to‑organic phase volume ratio is 40:1, then shake the mixture vigorously for 10–15 seconds; under these conditions cobalt(II) is extracted with ≈99.9 % efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare masking buffer solution
steps.instruction: Make a buffer of pH 3–5.5 containing 0.2 % (w/v) sodium nitrite. To this buffer add masking agents as required: sodium fluoride and thiourea to suppress Fe(III) and Bi(III) interference, additional thiourea to suppress Cu(II), and tartaric acid to suppress W(VI).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve sodium nitrite to give 0.2 % (w/v) in the buffer.
Adjust the buffer pH to between 3 and 5.5.
Add sodium fluoride (amount sufficient to mask Fe(III) and Bi(III)).
Add thiourea (amount sufficient to mask Fe(III), Bi(III) and Cu(II)).
Add tartaric acid (amount sufficient to mask W(VI)).

steps.title: Add PAN and develop colored complex
steps.instruction: To the chloroform extract add the PAN reagent together with the prepared buffer so that the extract : buffer+PAN volume ratio is 1:2, then shake the phases for another 10–15 seconds; a 1:2 cobalt‑PAN colored complex forms, stable for more than 3 days.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 640 nm
steps.instruction: Record the absorbance of the organic phase at the maximum wavelength of 640 nm; use the apparent molar absorption coefficient ε = 2 × 10⁴ L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹ and Beer’s law for quantification.
